questions.q: What is the main difference between a "give way" sign and a "stop" sign?
options: Stop always requires a full stop; give way requires slowing down and stopping only if necessary
The only difference is the colour of the sign
There is no difference — both require giving way
Give way requires a full stop; stop requires only slowing down
questions.explain: The stop sign (302) always requires a full stop, even when the junction is empty; the give-way sign (301) requires slowing down and stopping only if necessary (regs. 64(c)-(d)).

questions.q: What does "giving right of way" mean under the law?
options: To stop and wait for them to wave
To let the other road user keep moving without stopping, waiting, changing speed or deviating
To signal to the other road user that they may go
To drive ahead of them as long as you have not collided
questions.explain: Giving right of way means allowing another road user to keep moving without stopping, waiting, changing speed, or deviating from their line of travel (reg. 1).

questions.q: You are at a junction with legal right of way, but another driver is not letting you pass and is approaching. What should you do?
options: Sound the horn and continue, to teach them a lesson
Keep driving as usual — it is your right
Speed up to get past before them
Slow down or stop to prevent a crash, even if you are in the right
questions.explain: Right of way does not cancel the duty to prevent a crash. Even when the law is on your side, the responsibility to avoid a collision stays with you (reg. 51).

questions.q: A police officer is standing at a junction directing traffic by hand, while the traffic light at that junction shows red in your direction. Who do you obey?
options: The traffic light — it is fixed and more reliable
Whoever reached the junction first
Neither — you stop and wait for the officer to leave
The police officer — their instruction overrides the traffic light and the signs
questions.explain: Instructions from a police officer directing traffic override both the traffic light and the signs.

questions.q: You are approaching a junction with no sign and no traffic light. Another vehicle is approaching from your right at the same moment. Who gives way to whom?
options: Whoever is driving faster goes first
You give way to them — they are coming from your right
They give way to you — you arrived first
There is no priority when there is no sign — drive carefully and cross together
questions.explain: At a junction with no sign and no traffic light, right of way goes to the vehicle coming from the right (reg. 64(a)(1)).

questions.q: You reach a T-junction with no sign at all: your road ends at a wide road that continues straight in both directions. A vehicle is approaching from your right. Which rule applies?
options: There is no priority rule at all at a T-junction
You go first, because the wide road counts as less important
Priority to the right applies as usual — priority to the vehicle coming from your right
The vehicle on the wide road always has priority, because it is the main road
questions.explain: Priority to the right (reg. 64(a)(1)) applies at a T-junction too — based on the direction of arrival, not on which road looks like the main one. Because this causes confusion, there is almost always a sign there.

questions.q: You are driving out of a petrol station onto the road. What is the correct order of actions?
options: Sound the horn and pull out — a vehicle on the road has no priority over one leaving a petrol station
Slow down and make sure there are no pedestrians, and only then give way to the vehicle on the road
Priority to the right decides, exactly as at an ordinary junction
Give way to the vehicle on the road, and only then check for pedestrians
questions.explain: Leaving a petrol station does not count as a junction. First slow down and even stop to let pedestrians cross safely, and only then give way to any vehicle on the road (reg. 64(b)).

questions.q: A driver leaving a dirt road onto a paved road — what must they do?
options: Sound the horn twice before entering
Give way to a vehicle approaching on the paved road
Continue as normal, because a dirt road is not an official road
Give way only to a vehicle coming from their right
questions.explain: A driver leaving a dirt road onto a paved road, or crossing one, gives way to a vehicle approaching on the paved road (reg. 64(a)(3)).

questions.q: The traffic light is green, but the junction ahead of you is congested and you might get stuck in it before it turns red. What must you do?
options: Enter — the light is green, you are allowed to
Enter and stop inside the junction if necessary
Not enter the junction unless you can cross it and keep moving without being held up
Speed up to get through before it changes
questions.explain: You must not enter a junction unless you can cross it and keep moving without being held up — even on a green light (reg. 65).

questions.q: You are at a junction and intend to turn left. An oncoming vehicle is going straight on. Who has priority?
options: Neither — you both go through at the same time, carefully
You do — you are already at the junction
It depends who signalled first
The oncoming vehicle — it is going straight on
questions.explain: A driver intending to turn left or make a left U-turn gives way to the oncoming vehicle that is at the junction or close to it (reg. 64(a)(2)).

questions.q: Before turning right at a junction, what must you check in addition to the mirror?
options: That there is no vehicle behind you
Only the traffic light
That the oncoming vehicle has signalled
A direct look to the right — a cyclist or moped rider could be in your blind spot
questions.explain: Turning right is done from the right-hand edge and only when there is no vehicle moving on your right (reg. 42) — the mirror alone is not always enough to see a rider beside you.

questions.q: You gave way to the oncoming vehicle and you are turning left. At the last moment you notice a pedestrian crossing the road you are turning into. What must you do?
options: Continue — you already gave way to the oncoming vehicle
Sound the horn and continue slowly
Stop and give way to the pedestrian too
It is not relevant — only a vehicle can have right of way when turning
questions.explain: Giving way to the oncoming vehicle does not cancel the duty to give way to a pedestrian crossing the road you are turning into (reg. 67, and reg. 41, which allows turning only when it is safe).

questions.q: You are making a left U-turn at a junction where it is allowed. An oncoming vehicle is going straight on. Who gives way to whom?
options: You give way to the oncoming vehicle
The oncoming vehicle gives way to you
There is no special rule for a U-turn
It depends which of you is bigger
questions.explain: A left U-turn at a junction is subject to the same duty as an ordinary left turn: give way to the oncoming vehicle (reg. 64(a)(2)).

questions.q: At a junction with no sign, you want to turn left. There is both a vehicle coming from your right and an oncoming vehicle going straight on. Who do you give way to?
options: Both — priority to the right and giving way to the oncoming vehicle apply together
Only the vehicle on your right
Only the oncoming vehicle
Neither — you turn first because you have been waiting the longest
questions.explain: The duty to give way to the oncoming vehicle when turning left adds to priority to the right, and does not cancel it (reg. 64(a)(2)).

questions.q: You are approaching a roundabout with sign 303, and another vehicle is already inside the roundabout. Who enters first?
options: Whoever signals first
It depends who comes from the right
The vehicle already in the roundabout — it has priority
You — if you arrived before it finished going round
questions.explain: When entering a roundabout with sign 303, right of way belongs to the vehicle already inside the roundabout (reg. 64(g)).

questions.q: Which way does traffic go round a roundabout in Israel?
options: It varies from roundabout to roundabout
Anti-clockwise
It depends on the size of the roundabout
Clockwise
questions.explain: In Israel you drive on the right, so traffic at a roundabout goes anti-clockwise.

questions.q: When is the right time to signal right when leaving a roundabout?
options: Only if there is a vehicle behind you
Just before your exit, so as not to confuse a vehicle waiting to enter
As soon as you enter the roundabout
There is no need to signal in a roundabout at all
questions.explain: Leaving a roundabout is a deviation from your line of travel that requires signalling with enough time in advance (reg. 58). Signalling too early can confuse a driver waiting to enter.

questions.q: A long lorry is beside you in a roundabout and drifts slightly into your lane partway through the turn. What should you do?
options: Sound the horn and stay in your lane
Speed up to get past it
Give it room — a long vehicle has a wider turning radius
Overtake it quickly before it blocks you
questions.explain: A long vehicle has a wider turning radius, and sometimes needs to use part of the next lane to complete the turn safely. Give it room.

questions.q: A pedestrian is crossing at a marked crossing ahead of you. What is your duty?
options: Slow down but keep driving carefully past them
Stop only if there is a traffic light there
Let them complete the crossing safely, and stop if necessary
Sound the horn so they hurry up
questions.explain: A driver approaching a crossing where pedestrians are crossing must let them complete the crossing safely, and if necessary must stop (reg. 67(a)).

questions.q: A pedestrian is standing on the pavement near a crossing, and clearly about to cross. They have not stepped onto the road yet. What is correct?
options: You may continue — they are still on the pavement
Only at night, when visibility is poor
Only if they raise a hand
You must slow down and give them right of way already now
questions.explain: Even a pedestrian still standing on the pavement near a crossing, clearly intending to cross, already has right of way (reg. 67(a1)).

questions.q: You are driving on a two-lane road in one direction, approaching a crossing, and the vehicle in the other lane has stopped ahead of you. You cannot see why. What should you do?
options: Sound the horn for it to move
Continue in your lane — it is not in your lane
Slow down and stop too — there may be a pedestrian you cannot see
Overtake it from the side and continue
questions.explain: When a vehicle in another lane has slowed or stopped before a crossing, you must slow down and stop too — there may be a pedestrian hidden from your view (reg. 67(a2)).

questions.q: You are driving near a school at dismissal time, and the speed limit on this stretch is {{fact:speed.urban}}. What is correct?
options: Drive at {{fact:speed.urban}} — that is the speed limit
Drive at {{fact:speed.urban}} only if you actually see children
Slow down well below the speed limit, because a child might run onto the road
Speed up to get through the area quickly
questions.explain: Near children you must slow down significantly, regardless of the speed limit on the sign — it is only an upper limit (regs. 51-52).

questions.q: You hear a siren and see a flashing light approaching from behind. What must you do?
options: Continue at your normal speed until it overtakes
Speed up to clear the way for it faster
Stop where you are, even inside a junction
Steer right as close as possible to the edge of the road, away from a junction, and stop until it has passed
questions.explain: When an emergency vehicle approaches, drivers steer right as close as possible to the edge of the road, away from a junction, and stop there until it has passed (reg. 93(a)).

questions.q: What is the minimum gap you must keep when driving behind an emergency vehicle?
options: {{fact:following.security_vehicle_gap}}
20 metres
Like any other vehicle — one second
There is no special minimum gap
questions.explain: You must not follow an emergency vehicle at a gap smaller than {{fact:following.security_vehicle_gap}} (reg. 93(b)).

questions.q: A bus signals and prepares to leave a stop ahead of you. Who is legally required to make sure the departure is safe?
options: The bus driver themselves, before entering the flow of traffic
Only the vehicle behind the bus
The police, if present
No one — the bus has automatic priority
questions.explain: A driver moving a vehicle that was standing at the side of the road must first make sure they can enter the flow of traffic without risk or obstruction — this duty applies to a bus leaving a stop too (reg. 66).

questions.q: A lawful funeral procession moves as a continuous block on the road, with no gaps between vehicles. Is this an offence?
options: No — a funeral procession and a parade are exempt from the duty to leave gaps
Yes, unless it has a police escort
Yes — every convoy must leave gaps for a faster vehicle
Only if it is travelling on an urban road
questions.explain: An ordinary convoy on a non-urban road must leave gaps for a faster vehicle (reg. 50(a)), but a lawful funeral procession or parade is exempt from this duty (reg. 50(c)).

questions.q: Two vehicles meet from opposite directions on a road too narrow for both, with no sign at all. What must they do?
options: Whoever arrived first continues, the other stops
Both slow down and move right as far as possible, even beyond the edge of the carriageway if necessary
Whoever is in the bigger vehicle continues
Priority to the right decides
questions.explain: On a road too narrow for two directions, both drivers reduce speed and move right as far as possible until they are safe from collision (reg. 46(a)).

questions.q: Two vehicles meet on a steep, narrow road, and one of them must stop to allow passage. Which one stops?
options: The vehicle going downhill
Whoever reached the point first
Whoever is in the heavier vehicle
The vehicle going uphill
questions.explain: On a steep road, when circumstances require one vehicle to stop — the vehicle going downhill is the one that stops (reg. 46(b)). It is easier for the downhill vehicle to brake and wait.

questions.q: On a narrow stretch of road, a "give way to oncoming traffic" sign is placed. What does it mean?
options: The sign only applies to heavy vehicles
You go first, because you are going uphill
Both directions slow down and move right equally, as usual
You must give way to a vehicle coming from the opposite direction, regardless of the slope
questions.explain: Sign 307 explicitly states that traffic in your direction gives way to a vehicle coming from the opposite direction — regardless of the road's slope.

questions.q: A single-lane road is partly blocked by roadworks, leaving room to pass in only one direction. There is no police officer, flagger or sign present. Who gives way to whom?
options: Priority to the right decides
Whoever's lane is blocked gives way to the vehicle coming from the opposite direction
The bigger vehicle continues
Whoever reached the blockage first continues
questions.explain: A blocked road with room to pass in only one direction: whoever's lane is blocked gives way to the vehicle coming from the opposite direction, when there is no police officer, flagger, or sign directing otherwise (reg. 68).
